passages.title: Check the explanation
passages.text: AHRQ describes asking people to explain in their own words, taking responsibility for clarity, using small segments, clarifying and checking again. An acknowledgement is not the same as an account of the plan.
passages.context: Original bounded summary of the dated source reading; see source scope and limits.

passages.title: Language support is part of the task
passages.text: AHRQ distinguishes spoken and written preferences and qualified language support. Interpreting and written translation are different functions. Repeating English does not resolve every access need.
passages.context: Original bounded summary of the dated source reading; see source scope and limits.

passages.title: Original appointment card
passages.text: Fictional visit: Tuesday at 10:00, Room B. Bring a written list of questions. If unable to attend, contact the fictional reception desk. No real appointment or treatment instructions are represented.
passages.context: Original fictional scenario; associated source supplies a method/context only, not these facts.

passages.title: Original reply set
passages.text: Reply A: Yes, fine. Reply B: So I come at two to Room Ten? Reply C: Tuesday, ten, Room B—but I do not know where Room B is. Reply D: I will come Tuesday at ten to Room B, bring my questions, and contact reception if I cannot attend.
passages.context: Original fictional scenario; associated source supplies a method/context only, not these facts.

passages.title: Original clarification and recheck
passages.text: A possible response to B: I made that confusing. The time is ten in the morning; the room is B. Could you tell me when and where you would come? A scripted next reply is: Tuesday at ten, Room B. This is authored dialogue, not an observed learning result.
passages.context: Original fictional scenario; associated source supplies a method/context only, not these facts.

passages.title: Original access branch
passages.text: The person asks to use another spoken language and receive the written reminder in that language. No interpreter, translator or translated reminder has yet been supplied in this fictional file.
passages.context: Original fictional scenario; associated source supplies a method/context only, not these facts.

claims.text: Distinguish acknowledgement from an account of the plan.
claims.qualification: Original nonurgent scheduling dialogue informed by AHRQ communication tools. No diagnosis, treatment instruction, patient encounter, verified translation or comprehension outcome is supplied.

lenses.label: Find what is absent
lenses.observation: Reply A acknowledges; B confuses fields; C states a practical uncertainty; D restates the card.
lenses.question: What next move responds to each reply?
readings: For A, invite an own-words account instead of assuming the whole plan was understood.
For B, clarify time and room; for C, address the location question rather than simply reciting the card again.
lenses.boundary: Do not score intelligence, politeness or compliance from these replies.

lenses.label: Respond and check again
lenses.observation: The revised explanation is followed by a scripted restatement.
lenses.question: What claim does that restatement support within this exercise?
readings: It matches the authored time and room fields.
It does not establish future attendance, treatment understanding or a real person’s comprehension.
lenses.boundary: The script is not participant evidence.

lenses.label: Separate two language needs
lenses.observation: The access branch requests both spoken support and a written reminder.
lenses.question: What remains to be arranged before assuming the exchange is accessible?
readings: Recognize the need for appropriate qualified spoken support.
Treat the written translation as a separate task; do not call generated wording verified.
lenses.boundary: This lesson supplies no clinical translation or current legal compliance decision.

activity.transfer: Write a non-shaming response to C and a follow-up question that addresses the actual uncertainty. Then state one outcome that a correct scripted reply still cannot prove.
rubric: Distinguish acknowledgement from an account of the plan.
Address the specific uncertainty and check again.
Keep language support and written translation explicit.
Separate scripted correspondence from observed understanding.
